problem_context.title: Container With Most Water
problem_context.statement: Given an array height where height[i] is the height of a vertical line at position i, choose two lines that, with the horizontal axis, hold the greatest amount of water. Return that maximum area.

examples.explanation: The lines at positions 1 and 8 give height 7 across width 7.
The only pair has width 1 and limiting height 1.

expected_approaches.summary: Start at both ends and move inward only from a shorter boundary after evaluating the area.
expected_approaches.applicability: Ordered positions where area depends on distance and the smaller endpoint height.
key_invariants: Discarding the shorter boundary cannot remove a better pair using that boundary because width only decreases and the limiting height cannot improve unless that boundary changes.
tradeoffs: Requires a proof of the discard rule rather than a greedy height-only intuition.
common_implementation_variants: move either side on equal heights
common_failure_modes: using max height instead of min height

alternative_approaches.applicability: Only small inputs or a correctness baseline.
key_invariants: Every possible container pair is examined.
tradeoffs: Direct but not suitable for the largest inputs.

reference_solutions.source_code: class Solution { public: int maxArea(vector<int> height){ int left=0,right=height.size()-1,best=0; while(left<right){ best=max(best,(right-left)*min(height[left],height[right])); if(height[left]<height[right]) left++; else right--; } return best; } };

class Solution { public int maxArea(int[] height){ int left=0,right=height.length-1,best=0; while(left<right){best=Math.max(best,(right-left)*Math.min(height[left],height[right])); if(height[left]<height[right]) left++; else right--;} return best; } }

invariants.diagnostic_goal: Moving the shorter line is safe because keeping it only narrows width while retaining the same height limit.

complexity_expectations.diagnostic_goal: Each iteration advances exactly one boundary.

common_misconceptions.diagnostic_goal: Area depends on both width and the shorter height.

failure_modes.diagnostic_goal: Do not discard the boundary that could still improve the limiting height.

edge_cases.diagnostic_goal: The only pair must be evaluated.

counterexamples.purpose: Always moving the taller endpoint discards index 3 immediately and misses the optimal pair at indices 1 and 3.
The tallest line does not determine the optimum: the shorter outer lines hold area 3, while any pair using height 10 holds at most area 2.

constraint_mutations.diagnostic_goal: Either boundary may move when heights tie, provided progress is made.

probe_opportunities.diagnostic_goal: Compare exhaustive pairs with the pointer proof.

expected_good_signals: explains width decreases while short height remains limiting
weak_or_misconception_signals: moves the taller line by intuition
sample_phrasings: Why can no better container still use the shorter boundary?
What must happen when both endpoint heights are equal?
Which two quantities determine the area of a chosen pair?

level_considerations.guidance: Prioritize a sound shorter-side discard proof.
